tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Analyticity] ↗ thm:harmonic-function-derivative-estimates ↗ thm:harmonic-functions-smooth 1. ch2:2.2-thm-10\group Harmonic Functions

Every harmonic function is analytic in its domain.
Proof

\sketch Fix $x_0\in U$, put $r=\dist (x_0,\partial U)/4$, and set $M=[\alpha (n)r^n]^{-1}\| u\| _{L^1(B(x_0,2r))}$. The derivative estimate, Stirling’s formula [RD, §8.22], and the multinomial theorem give

\[ (22)\qquad \| D^\alpha u\| _{L^\infty (B(x_0,r))} \le CM\left(\frac{2^{n+1}n^2e}{r}\right)^{|\alpha |}\alpha !. \]

Taylor’s formula along $t\mapsto u(x_0+t(x-x_0))$ then bounds the degree-$N$ remainder by $CM2^{-N}$ whenever $|x-x_0|<r/(2^{n+2}n^3e)$. Hence the Taylor series converges to $u$ near $x_0$.

□
